stem:
Rekha must walk from house $H$ to a straight path $L$, then to shop $S$. She wants the shortest broken path $H$-$P$-$S$ with $P$ on $L$.

Which claims correctly describe how to choose $P$? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The answer is the path $L$ itself, so every point on $L$ gives the same shortest length.
Reflect $S$ across $L$ to $S'$, then choose $P$ where segment $HS'$ meets $L$.
That point $P$ makes $H$-$P$-$S$ equal in length to the straight segment $HS'$.
Choose $P$ as the foot of the perpendicular from the midpoint of $HS$ onto $L$.

teacher.key_rationale: Reflect one endpoint across the line and join the other endpoint to the image; the intersection with the line is the shortest broken-path point, and that broken length equals the straight segment to the image. Not every point on L works, and the midpoint perpendicular foot is a different construction.
